comments.value:
This is literally my most requested feature to add out of the 20+ mods I use to run. 
It enables me to go from sub 10fps in club worlds / large gatherings to over 40, and it's better than the safety feature of turning everyone into robots because robots are just not fun to look at, they're just not. I can have everyone's base model shown in my safety settings, and only when I come into distance with them do I render their avatar at all. Meaning I don't have to constantly fiddle with settings, allowing avatars etc, when I move around / change worlds just in order to see them. It's also incredibly useful if you want to sit at the back of a club / large group of people and see through them, only viewing the performers at the front, as anyone past the set distance doesn't render.
It has no negative affects for VRC, hiding someone else's avatar doesn't cause a detriment to game worlds / other people in any way, if anything it would just hurt you.
This is what this feature needs:
- It needs to have a variable distance slider / numeric input.
- Always show the nameplates, even when the avatar is hidden.
- The hidden avatars are still selectable / hearable, etc. It's just the rendering of the model that is stopped.
- Showing avatars will bypass the distance based hiding
- Ability to allow friends to bypass distance based hiding

I never join on my friends in 40+ player instances because the lag is crazy.
This is a good optimization option.
@{60cb78838b5c3f1e8f8fddf1|full_name}: I feel like the nameplates should be an option. That's extra rendering that personally, I don't care about seeing. But everything else is spot on!
I personaly agree this feature, even tought a bit redunded, would add a bigg performance boost to the game overall for all the people that run on toasters, like me
I feel like this could also be addressed by the following request: https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/better-playeravatar-culling-for-large-instances

@{60cb78838b5c3f1e8f8fddf1|full_name}: Yes, this exactly. Everything you said. This one basic, no-brainer, easy to implement feature singlehandedly MAKES the difference between whether public worlds and especially clubs are only viable for people with very high-end PCs (current situation), vs. open to most everyone.
My system isn't even a potato. It's actually very powerful. But not powerful enough to show more than just my friends at a club. I'm currently stranded in the middle of nowhere (super rural area), transitioning, and recovering from a debilitating injury, and I love music. I really need to be able to meet new people in clubs. That's way way harder to do if I don't even get to really see any strangers without showing their avatars one by one and being careful to hide anyone I'm not still talking to (so that I don't end up showing too many at once). I had this already solved before the crazy devs decided to take away functionality like this that so many of us depend on, instead of implementing it BEFORE implementing EAC. Y'all need to rush this out ASAP if you're really committed to EAC now.

This feature in mods was extremely useful and gave noticeble big performance boost. Even if some avatar's state machines got broken, it was worth it. Must-have in large instance where every CPU millisecond is important.

@{5f8a26770aaa28611fedd6b6|full_name}: Disagree, while better culling would probably be useful, it still would not have the drastic FPS increase this feature has. If I'm sitting at the back looking towards 70 people, better culling won't do a single thing to help my fps. Giving me what is essentially an inverted safety bubble, however, would.

I don't think the two requests are mutually exclusive! It very much depends on the type of world you're in.
**Avatar range limits** would lessen GPU load (by rendering fewer players). That's good for DJ events, or worlds that are like big boxes: I can see everyone at once, there's nowhere to hide.
And **better culling** would decrease CPU load (no collision, audio, etc). That's good for any world with rooms, walls and different areas. Most players are already hidden by Unity's occlusion culling system, but my CPU is still running a lot of code for those players.
**Both** would help! 😁
Personally, I kind of like being able to see 80 people at once. If a world creator did not want me to do that, they could have designed their world differently, or lowered the max player cap. I'd also want to avoid situations where someone waves at me, but I had them hidden!
**Edit**: VRChat's most recent blog post announced that they'll let us do both. Nice.

Sliders should not only go up to 50m and 30 Avatars. In Bigger worlds i might want to see further away than 50m but not infinity far. Same with  how many avatars i wanna show. with more performant PC i might be able to show more than 30 Avatars but not 80. Would be nice to adjust slider range up to 80.
I think the nametags should still stay or make it optional. I most certainly would like to know if someone's lurking just ouside the render range.

details:
Please add the feature to hide avatars (no robot, no nameplate, no render, nothing) outside a certain distance. It'd be nice if you could filter that and ignore friends, or only hide Very Poors.
This will help framerate immensely in instances with many people.
title: Hide Avatars In Range
